b:
When the morning sun
in an excess of love
sweeps them into his arms,
the white horses,
worn out by his hot embrace,
run away from him
and press their lips
to the shore sand
where her footprints lie,
and find comfort there

The full moon too,
lovesick
for her beauty,
hides
in the clouds
and gazes down
upon her

The cool wind
that slips through
the strands of her hair
makes even the song
of the distant cuckoos
forgotten

As a part of nature
I too admire her,

her
lover
beyond her imagining
note: The "white horses" are the white-crested waves of the sea.
